public.summary: Three clubs share one study room across three days. Find a schedule that follows every rule.
public.statement: The Maple Harbor library has one bookable study room. Three student clubs — Robotics, Chess, and Poetry — each need it for one afternoon this week. The room is free on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Assign each club to a day so that every rule below is followed.
facts: The room is available Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday afternoons only.
The Robotics mentor works at another site on Mondays.

constraints.text: Each club gets exactly one day, and each day hosts exactly one club.
Chess must meet on an earlier day than Poetry.

answer_format.instructions: Choose which club uses the room on each day.

public.explanation_prompt: How did you narrow down the days? Which rule did you use first?

provenance.author: Reasoning Lab project team
provenance.contamination_note: Original task. Its structure resembles common scheduling logic puzzles, so a model may have seen similar patterns.

anchors.constraints: 0 = not stated; 1 = rule mentioned; 2 = rule applied to eliminate a placement

reviewed_explanation.text: Poetry cannot be on Wednesday, and Chess must come before Poetry, so Poetry cannot be on Monday either (nothing would be earlier). Poetry is therefore on Tuesday and Chess on Monday. That leaves Wednesday for Robotics, which also respects the no-Monday rule. This is the only schedule that follows every rule.
reviewed_explanation.accepted_summary: Monday Chess, Tuesday Poetry, Wednesday Robotics (unique).

review.notes: Uniqueness confirmed by bounded enumeration in tests/unit/seeds.test.ts.
